meta.name: god-mode-codex-taxonomy
meta.description: Universal taxonomy of software-engineering meta-concepts, language constructs, patterns, principles, framework conventions and tooling — the knowledge base for an all-language convention-deriving dev tool (Chameleon-style, god mode).

sections.C: Design patterns, architecture styles, principles, code smells, refactorings, testing/concurrency/distributed patterns
sections.E: Tooling layer: parsers, codemods, code intelligence, universal rule schema, enforcement

concepts.definition: An agreed way of doing things that is not enforced by the language itself; consistency matters more than the specific choice.
concepts.detection_hint: Infer statistically: if most files matching a glob share a structure or choice, treat it as a convention and flag outliers.
concepts.example: Next.js route files under app/api/ exporting functions named GET and POST.

concepts.definition: A rule is a specific checkable do/don't statement, the atomic unit of governance; a lint rule is that idea encoded in a static-analysis tool so violations are flagged or auto-fixed mechanically.
concepts.detection_hint: AST pattern plus config file (.eslintrc, pyproject.toml [tool.ruff]); each rule has an ID, severity, and message.
concepts.example: ESLint no-unused-vars; Clippy needless_return in Rust.

concepts.definition: A formally published agreement by a recognized standards body; compliance enables interoperability between different vendors and tools.
concepts.detection_hint: Compliance test suites (e.g., Test262 for JavaScript); verify code parses and behaves per the published grammar.
concepts.example: ECMA-262 defines JavaScript; ISO/IEC 9075 defines SQL.

concepts.definition: The authoritative written description of what a system, language, or API must do; the source of truth implementations are checked against.
concepts.detection_hint: Contract tests generated from machine-readable specs (OpenAPI, protobuf); verify responses match the schema.
concepts.example: An OpenAPI YAML file describing every endpoint of a REST API.

concepts.definition: A written document fixing formatting, naming, and layout choices so all code looks like one person wrote it.
concepts.detection_hint: Formatters enforce it automatically (black, prettier, gofmt, rustfmt); violations are auto-fixable.
concepts.example: PEP 8 for Python; Google Style Guides; Airbnb JavaScript Style Guide.

concepts.definition: A policy is an official organizational rule (often security or legal driven); a mandate is a non-negotiable one; governance is the whole system of policies, enforcement, and ownership.
concepts.detection_hint: Policy-as-code engines (Open Policy Agent/Rego, Sentinel, Checkov) enforced at CI or admission-control time.
concepts.example: Secrets may never be committed; all dependencies must come from the internal Artifactory mirror.

concepts.definition: An explicit list of forbidden (or exclusively permitted) APIs, dependencies, patterns, or words; older terms: blacklist/whitelist.
concepts.detection_hint: Import-graph scanning plus AST call-site search; e.g., ESLint no-restricted-imports, dependency-cruiser rules.
concepts.example: Ban eval() and lodash; only allow image hosts listed in next.config.js remotePatterns.

concepts.definition: A design philosophy where the framework assumes sensible defaults from naming and placement conventions, so you only write config when you deviate.
concepts.detection_hint: Read the framework's conventional locations (Rails app/models, Django models.py) to locate things without config files.
concepts.example: Rails maps a Post model to the posts table automatically, zero config.

concepts.definition: Configuration is explicit settings that change behavior without changing code; defaults are the values used when you configure nothing.
concepts.detection_hint: Parse config files (JSON/YAML/TOML/INI, .env); diff effective config against defaults to find the team's real choices.
concepts.example: tsconfig.json strict: true; Prettier's default 80-char print width.

concepts.definition: A recurring kind of file, class, or module within one codebase: a cluster of code units sharing role, structure, and naming. Discovered by analysis, not decreed.
concepts.detection_hint: Cluster files by structural features (imports, decorators, exported symbols, AST shape); each dense cluster is an archetype.
concepts.example: Spring Boot repo: Controller, Service, and Repository archetypes, each with its own annotation set.

concepts.definition: The single standard shape something should be in, so comparisons and tooling are trivial; canonical means the officially preferred form.
concepts.detection_hint: Normalizers like gofmt put all files in canonical form; canonicalize then diff, and any diff is a deviation.
concepts.example: Canonical JSON with sorted keys and no whitespace, used for hashing.

concepts.definition: The single best real file chosen as the living proof of an archetype: if you must imitate one file, imitate this one. Chameleon's term.
concepts.detection_hint: Score each cluster member (recency, test coverage, convention adherence, review approval); pick the best as witness and inject it as few-shot context before AI edits.
concepts.example: billing/invoice.service.ts is the canonical witness for the Service archetype.

concepts.definition: An exemplar is any high-quality instance worth copying; a reference implementation is the official working implementation of a spec used to judge all others.
concepts.detection_hint: Chosen by authority (spec body) or quality metrics; conformance suites compare other implementations against the reference.
concepts.example: CPython is the reference implementation of Python.

concepts.definition: The golden path is the officially supported, recommended way to accomplish something in an ecosystem; the happy path is the scenario where nothing goes wrong (no errors or edge cases).
concepts.detection_hint: Scaffold templates and docs encode the golden path; happy-path tests assert the success branch exists per feature.
concepts.example: New services here are created from the Kotlin/Spring template on Backstage.

concepts.definition: A pre-written skeleton with placeholder slots you fill in; guarantees every new instance starts identical.
concepts.detection_hint: Detect duplicated boilerplate with variable holes (high token overlap); generators like Plop/Hygen store templates in the repo.
concepts.example: A GitHub PR template with Summary and Testing sections; a Jinja2 template Hello {{name}}.

concepts.definition: Code that must be repeated nearly verbatim in many places to satisfy the language or framework, adding little new information; usually mildly derogatory.
concepts.detection_hint: Clone detection (PMD CPD, jscpd) finds high-duplication regions; high boilerplate suggests a missing abstraction or macro.
concepts.example: Java getters/setters; public static void main(String[] args).

concepts.definition: Starting-point artifacts: a scaffold is auto-generated starter code for a component; a starter is a runnable minimal project; a blueprint is the reusable generator definition; cookiecutter is the Python tool that popularized project templates; a sample is small demo code showing usage.
concepts.detection_hint: Generator configs (cookiecutter.json, plopfile.js); doc-code extraction from READMEs and samples/ dirs; compile samples in CI to keep them honest.
concepts.example: rails generate scaffold Post; npx create-next-app; Stripe SDK's example/ folder.

concepts.definition: A real instance of the wrong way, shown side-by-side with the right way so the contrast teaches the rule; Chameleon pairs one with every idiom.
concepts.detection_hint: Mine from reverted commits, code-review comments (don't do X), and historical lint violations; store as bad-to-good pairs.
concepts.example: Next to with open(...), show f = open(...); f.read() with no close() and explain the leaked handle.

concepts.definition: A named, reusable solution to a recurring design problem, described by intent, structure, and trade-offs; known industry-wide, independent of any one codebase.
concepts.detection_hint: Structural matching: look for the pattern's signature (e.g., Subject with subscribe/notify plus an Observer list).
concepts.example: Strategy pattern: swap sorting algorithms by injecting a comparator.

concepts.definition: The natural, community-preferred way to express a small common task in one language; instantly recognizable to natives of that language.
concepts.detection_hint: Frequency mining: count AST fragments across the corpus; high-frequency fragments that beat alternatives become idiom candidates.
concepts.example: Python [x*2 for x in xs]; Go if err != nil { return err }; Rust ? operator.

concepts.definition: An overall style or philosophy of programming defining what programs are made of and how they run: object-oriented, functional, procedural, declarative, logic, reactive.
concepts.detection_hint: Feature detection: pervasive classes plus inheritance (OOP) vs immutable data plus map/filter/reduce (FP) reveals the dominant paradigm.
concepts.example: Java is object-oriented; Haskell purely functional; SQL declarative.

concepts.definition: Hiding messy details behind a simpler named interface so users think in terms of what, not how; the core move of all software design.
concepts.detection_hint: Layer analysis: call graphs where high-level modules never import low-level details indicate healthy abstraction; leaky imports signal violations.
concepts.example: users.findById(id) hides SQL, pooling, and caching behind one name.

concepts.definition: A construct is any syntactic feature of a language (if, for, class); a primitive is the smallest built-in thing you cannot decompose (int, boolean); building block is informal for any basic reusable piece.
concepts.detection_hint: The language grammar enumerates all constructs as AST node types; primitives appear as the type system's base types.
concepts.example: Go primitives: int, string, channels; constructs: switch, defer.

concepts.definition: A self-contained, reusable unit with a defined interface: in UI a visual building block; in architecture a deployable or pluggable part of a system.
concepts.detection_hint: UI: files exporting JSX/.vue/.svelte components; architecture: dependency-graph boundaries with well-defined public APIs.
concepts.example: React <Button variant="primary">; the payment component in a microservices diagram.

concepts.definition: A file or cohesive group that encapsulates related code behind explicit imports and exports; the unit of code organization within one program.
concepts.detection_hint: The import/export graph is the module structure; analyze cycles, coupling, and public vs private surface.
concepts.example: export function formatDate() plus import { formatDate } from './date'.

concepts.definition: A versioned, distributable bundle of modules with metadata (name, version, dependencies), published to a registry.
concepts.detection_hint: Manifest files (package.json, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, go.mod) declare packages; lockfiles pin exact versions.
concepts.example: npm install lodash; Rust crate serde on crates.io.

concepts.definition: A library is reusable code you call (your code stays in control); a framework is a skeleton application that calls you via hooks (inversion of control). Same dependency mechanism, opposite direction of control.
concepts.detection_hint: Direction of call-graph edges: your code to library (library) vs framework invoking your callbacks and handlers (framework).
concepts.example: Lodash is a library you call; Django is a framework that calls your views.

concepts.definition: A toolkit is a set of related tools and libraries for one domain; an SDK is a vendor's official bundle (libraries plus docs plus tools) for building on their platform.
concepts.detection_hint: Published packages whose names contain sdk or toolkit; detected via dependencies and vendor-branded APIs.
concepts.example: AWS SDK for JavaScript; Android SDK; Redux Toolkit.

concepts.definition: Application Programming Interface: the published surface through which one piece of software talks to another (function signatures, endpoints, or protocols); what you may call and what you get back.
concepts.detection_hint: Public-export analysis (exported vs internal); OpenAPI/protobuf files define network APIs; semver tracks API changes.
concepts.example: Stripe REST API POST /v1/charges; the DOM API document.querySelector.

concepts.definition: Domain-Specific Language: a small language tailored to one problem area; internal DSLs are hosted inside a general language, external DSLs have their own syntax and parser.
concepts.detection_hint: External: distinct file extensions and grammars (.sql, .graphql); internal: tell-tale chained call patterns and builder APIs.
concepts.example: External: SQL, regex, CSS; internal: RSpec describe/it blocks, Gradle Kotlin DSL.

concepts.definition: Writing code that reads, generates, or transforms other code (or itself) at compile or runtime; macros and code generation are its main mechanisms.
concepts.detection_hint: Decorator/attribute usage rates, macro invocations, generated-file markers (Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT).
concepts.example: Python decorators; Ruby method_missing; Rust derive(Debug).

concepts.definition: A metaprogramming construct that expands code at compile or preprocess time: you write shorthand, the compiler writes the verbose version.
concepts.detection_hint: Preprocessor directives (#define), bang-suffixed calls in Rust (println!), attribute macros; all visible to the parser.
concepts.example: C #define MAX(a,b); Rust #[derive(Serialize)].

concepts.definition: A program examining (introspection) and modifying (reflection) its own structure at runtime: classes, methods, types.
concepts.detection_hint: Calls to reflection APIs (java.lang.reflect, getattr, Type.GetType) are statically detectable and often flagged in audits.
concepts.example: Python getattr(obj, name); Java obj.getClass().getMethods().

concepts.definition: Code generation: programs that write source files from schemas or templates, so repetitive code is never hand-written.
concepts.detection_hint: Generated files carry header markers; build configs list codegen steps; tools should not lint generated code as team style.
concepts.example: protoc emits typed classes from .proto files; GraphQL codegen emits TypeScript types.

concepts.definition: A formal agreement attached to a function or module: what callers must guarantee and what the callee guarantees back, making assumptions explicit and checkable.
concepts.detection_hint: Assertion statements (assert, require, ensure), JML/OpenJML annotations, or TypeScript types serving as machine-checkable contracts.
concepts.example: Requires a non-empty list and promises a sorted result.

concepts.definition: A named set of method signatures a class or struct promises to provide, with no implementation; the decoupling tool: code to the interface, not the implementation.
concepts.detection_hint: implements/extends clauses; Go structural check (a type satisfies an interface by having the methods); DI containers bind interfaces to implementations.
concepts.example: TypeScript interface UserRepo { find(id: string): Promise<User> }.

concepts.definition: Two meanings: (1) a network protocol, rules for machines exchanging messages; (2) a code protocol, an interface-like capability contract (Swift, Objective-C, Python).
concepts.detection_hint: Network: .proto files and protocol parsers; code: protocol keyword or duck-typing conventions (Python dunder methods).
concepts.example: HTTP (network); Swift protocol Equatable; Python's iterator protocol __iter__/__next__.

concepts.definition: A bundle of methods and types mixed into types to give them a capability; like interfaces, but often with default implementations and retroactive extension of existing types.
concepts.detection_hint: impl Trait for Type blocks enumerate capabilities; the compiler checks trait bounds on generics (T: Clone).
concepts.example: Rust impl Display for User; Haskell instance Eq User.

concepts.definition: The shape of a function: its name, parameter types and order, and return type; everything a caller needs to know, without the body.
concepts.detection_hint: Extracted trivially from AST declarations; signature-diffing across versions detects breaking API changes (semver tooling).
concepts.example: function fetchUser(id: string, opts?: CacheOpts): Promise<User>.

concepts.definition: A precondition is what must be true before a call (caller's duty); a postcondition is what is guaranteed after (callee's duty); an invariant is what must always be true of a data structure before and after every operation.
concepts.detection_hint: require/ensure clauses, Kotlin require(), assertion density; property-based tests (Hypothesis, fast-check) hunt invariant violations.
concepts.example: Pre: amount > 0; invariant: a BST's left children are always smaller.

concepts.definition: A formal description of the shape of data: fields, types, requiredness, allowed values; for databases, JSON, messages, or configs.
concepts.detection_hint: Schema files are machine-readable by definition; validators (ajv, pydantic, zod, protobuf compilers) check data against them.
concepts.example: PostgreSQL CREATE TABLE users (...); Prisma schema.prisma; JSON Schema required: [email].

concepts.definition: Validation is checking data against a schema or rules and rejecting what fails; a constraint is a single rule data must satisfy (unique, non-null, range, format).
concepts.detection_hint: Validators declared in schemas or decorators (@IsEmail in NestJS); DB constraints visible in migrations; fuzzers probe constraint edges.
concepts.example: zod z.string().email().min(5); Django unique=True.

concepts.definition: Writing code once with a placeholder type so it works for many types while staying type-safe; called generics in most languages, templates in C++.
concepts.detection_hint: Angle-bracket and type-parameter syntax in declarations; monomorphization (Rust/C++) or erasure (Java) visible at compile time.
concepts.example: function identity<T>(x: T): T; Java List<String>; Rust Vec<T>.

concepts.definition: Static typing checks types at compile time (Java, Rust); dynamic checks at runtime (Python, JS); gradual allows optional annotations (TypeScript, Python+mypy). Type inference is the compiler deducing unwritten types from context.
concepts.detection_hint: Presence of a compile-time type checker; ratio of explicit annotations to inferred bindings measures how gradual the codebase is.
concepts.example: TypeScript const n = 5 infers number; Rust let v = vec![1,2] infers Vec<i32>.

concepts.definition: Nominal typing requires types to share a declared name or ancestry to be compatible (Java, C#); structural typing only requires the same shape (TypeScript interfaces, Go interfaces).
concepts.detection_hint: Assignability rules of the type checker; Go's implicit interface satisfaction is the canonical structural example.
concepts.example: TS: { name: string } is assignable to interface Named automatically; Java requires implements Named.

concepts.definition: A technique the community broadly agrees produces good outcomes in a given context; strong evidence-backed advice, but not a law, and context can override it.
concepts.detection_hint: Encoded as linter rules, security scanners (Semgrep rulesets), and checklist gates in CI.
concepts.example: Use parameterized SQL queries to prevent injection; pin dependencies with a lockfile.

concepts.definition: A commonly reinvented bad solution: a pattern-shaped mistake with a name, so teams can recognize and avoid it.
concepts.detection_hint: Structural signatures per anti-pattern: e.g., a class with very many methods and incoming dependencies is a God Object candidate.
concepts.example: God Object, Spaghetti Code, Golden Hammer, Copy-Paste Programming.

concepts.definition: A surface symptom that suggests (but does not prove) a deeper design problem: something looks off, look closer. Cataloged by Fowler and Beck.
concepts.detection_hint: Metric thresholds: method length, cyclomatic complexity, coupling counts, parameter count; each breach flags a smell.
concepts.example: Long Method, Large Class, Feature Envy, Primitive Obsession.

concepts.definition: Technical debt is the future cost incurred by a shortcut now (you pay interest in slower changes until you repay by cleaning up); code rot is quality decay over time as a codebase drifts from its design and environment.
concepts.detection_hint: Debt: TODO/FIXME/HACK mining, SonarQube debt ratios; rot: churn vs test-coverage decline, dependency freshness scores.
concepts.example: Hardcoded tax rate shipped Friday now blocks multi-country support; an untouched 2018 module whose deps are all deprecated.

concepts.definition: Changing code's internal structure without changing its external behavior; the repayment mechanism for debt and smells.
concepts.detection_hint: IDEs perform safe automated refactors; verifiable because tests must pass identically before and after.
concepts.example: Extract Method, Rename Variable, Move Function to its proper module.

concepts.definition: Umbrella term (popularized by Robert C. Martin) for code that is readable, simple, well-named, and easy to change; the positive ideal that smells and anti-patterns negate.
concepts.detection_hint: Aggregate of lint health, complexity metrics, naming-consistency checks, and duplication scores.
concepts.example: Functions under ~20 lines doing one thing; names like sendInvoiceEmail, not doStuff.

concepts.definition: A code smell where one logical change forces edits in many scattered places; a sign the concept was never given one home. Opposite smell: Divergent Change.
concepts.detection_hint: Commit-cluster analysis: files that repeatedly change together in the same commits (change coupling) flag shotgun-surgery risk.
concepts.example: Adding a User field requires touching the form, validator, DTO, migration, serializer, and 3 tests.

concepts.definition: A named, callable unit of code that takes parameters, does work, and usually returns a value; the fundamental unit of behavior in most languages.
concepts.detection_hint: Function declarations are first-class AST nodes; the call graph is built by resolving every call site to a declaration.
concepts.example: Python def add(a, b): return a + b; Go func Add(a, b int) int.

concepts.definition: A function attached to a class or object, called on an instance (or the class itself), with implicit access to the object's data via this/self.
concepts.detection_hint: Functions declared inside class/struct/impl blocks; a self/this first parameter marks method-ness.
concepts.example: Java user.getName(); Python class User: def rename(self, name): ...

concepts.definition: Older or general synonyms for a callable code unit; procedure historically stresses doing (maybe no return value) where function stresses returning a value.
concepts.detection_hint: Same AST detection as functions; in SQL, CREATE PROCEDURE vs CREATE FUNCTION (functions must return a value).
concepts.example: SQL stored procedure CALL calculate_payroll(); Visual Basic Sub.

concepts.definition: A function you hand to someone else so they call it later: call me back when X happens. The simplest inversion of control.
concepts.detection_hint: Functions passed as arguments to other calls; promise .then(...), event registrations.
concepts.example: JS button.addEventListener('click', () => close()); Node fs.readFile(path, (err, data) => ...).

concepts.definition: A designated extension point where a framework or library lets you inject your code into its process; includes lifecycle hooks and React-style composable Hooks.
concepts.detection_hint: Calls to known hook APIs (use[A-Z]* in React), hook files in .git/hooks/, registration calls in plugin systems.
concepts.example: React useEffect(() => {...}, [deps]); Git pre-commit hook scripts.

concepts.definition: The fixed sequence of stages a component, object, or app passes through from creation to destruction, each stage an opportunity to hook in.
concepts.detection_hint: Framework-defined method name sets (onCreate, componentDidMount, ngOnInit); tools check mandatory teardown hooks exist.
concepts.example: Android Activity: onCreate -> onStart -> onResume -> onPause -> onDestroy.

concepts.definition: Code that sits in the middle of a request/response or call flow, able to inspect, modify, short-circuit, or log, assembled in a chain; interceptor is the same idea in other frameworks.
concepts.detection_hint: Registration APIs (app.use, middleware stacks in config); chain order matters, so tools model the ordered pipeline per route.
concepts.example: Express app.use((req, res, next) => { log(req); next(); }); NestJS interceptors.

concepts.definition: A sequence of processing stages where each stage's output feeds the next, like an assembly line for data.
concepts.detection_hint: Chained calls and pipe operators; builder APIs returning transformed objects; dataflow graphs in stream frameworks.
concepts.example: Unix cat log | grep ERROR | wc -l; pandas df.dropna().groupby('k').mean().

concepts.definition: A function or object registered to respond to an event: handler (web/CLI), listener (Java/JS events), observer (GoF pattern); all mean code that reacts when something happens.
concepts.detection_hint: Route tables mapping URL to handler; addEventListener/@EventListener/subscribe registrations; observer lists in the Subject pattern.
concepts.example: Express app.get('/users', handler); JS element.addEventListener('scroll', listener).

concepts.definition: An event is a notification that something happened, carrying data, dispatched to whoever listens; a signal is the same idea in OS, Qt, or reactive contexts (often lightweight: something changed).
concepts.detection_hint: emit/dispatch/publish call sites paired with listener registrations; mine event-name strings for the system's event vocabulary.
concepts.example: Browser click event; Node EventEmitter.emit('order:created', order); OS SIGTERM.

concepts.definition: A coroutine is a function that can pause mid-execution and resume later where it left off (the basis of async programming without threads); a generator is a special coroutine producing a sequence of values lazily, one at a time.
concepts.detection_hint: async/suspend modifiers plus await points (coroutines); yield keyword (generators); compilers transform both into state machines.
concepts.example: Python async def fetch(): await client.get(url); def count(): yield 1; yield 2.

concepts.definition: A lambda is an anonymous function literal (no name); a closure is any function that captures variables from the scope where it was defined, keeping them alive. They often appear together.
concepts.detection_hint: Arrow functions and lambda tokens; closure detection = a function body referencing identifiers from an enclosing non-global scope.
concepts.example: JS const inc = (() => { let n = 0; return () => ++n; })() closes over n; Python lambda x: x*2.

concepts.definition: A function that takes functions as arguments and/or returns a function; functions treating functions as values.
concepts.detection_hint: Parameters and returns typed as function types; their density measures how functional a codebase is.
concepts.example: map(f, xs); JS const adder = a => b => a + b; Python sorted(users, key=lambda u: u.age).

concepts.definition: A pure function always returns the same output for the same input and touches nothing outside itself; a side effect is any observable interaction with the outside world (I/O, mutation, network, logging), making a function impure.
concepts.detection_hint: Effects analysis: calls to I/O, network, or global-mutation APIs inside a body mark it impure; React/Redux tools demand purity in reducers and render.
concepts.example: Pure: const square = x => x * x. Impure: function save(u) { db.insert(u); log('saved'); }.

concepts.definition: A function that calls itself (directly or via a cycle) to solve a problem by reducing it to smaller cases, stopping at a base case.
concepts.detection_hint: Call-graph cycles: an edge from a function back to itself; warn on missing base cases or unbounded recursion depth.
concepts.example: def fact(n): return 1 if n <= 1 else n * fact(n - 1); walking a directory tree.

concepts.definition: The agreed arrangement of folders and files in a project, often half framework-mandated and half team-chosen.
concepts.detection_hint: Framework detectors read known layouts; deviation analysis finds files placed outside every known archetype directory.
concepts.example: Next.js app/ routes + components/ + lib/; Maven src/main/java and src/test/java.

concepts.definition: Agreed casing and format rules for identifiers and files: snake_case (Python/Ruby/DB columns), camelCase (JS/Java variables and functions), PascalCase (classes, components, types), kebab-case (URLs, CSS classes, npm packages, many file names), SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (constants, env vars).
concepts.detection_hint: Regex per identifier class; linters enforce (eslint naming-convention, pep8-naming); file-name casing checked per directory.
concepts.example: Python class InvoiceService (Pascal), def get_total() (snake), TAX_RATE (screaming); React UserCard.tsx.

concepts.definition: A kind of file in a repo identified by naming, location, and internal structure: tests, configs, migrations, components, DTOs; the file-level version of the archetype concept.
concepts.detection_hint: Filename glob plus directory plus internal structure: name matches *.test.* and imports a test framework means test archetype.
concepts.example: *.test.ts (test), *.dto.ts (DTO), *_test.go (Go test), Dockerfile, *.migration.sql.

concepts.definition: A module system is the platform's mechanism for splitting code into importable units and resolving them (ESM, CommonJS, Go modules, Java packages); a namespace is a named container preventing identifier collisions.
concepts.detection_hint: Import resolution graph; package/namespace declarations; mixed ESM plus CJS in one repo is a detectable smell.
concepts.example: Node import x from './x.js' vs require('./x'); C# namespace Billing { class Invoice {} }.

concepts.definition: A monorepo is one repository holding many related projects or packages (opposite: polyrepo); a workspace is the tooling feature that links those packages for local development.
concepts.detection_hint: Root manifest listing workspace globs (pnpm-workspace.yaml, workspaces in package.json, go.work); cross-package internal dependency edges.
concepts.example: A repo with apps/web, apps/api, packages/ui managed by Turborepo.

concepts.definition: The central or private service where packages are published and downloaded from, with versioning and metadata.
concepts.detection_hint: Registry URLs in manifests and lockfiles; publishConfig; audit provenance and private-vs-public dependency confusion.
concepts.example: npmjs.com, PyPI, crates.io, Maven Central; private: GitHub Packages, Artifactory.

concepts.definition: A workflow is the defined sequence of steps (human and automated) work follows from start to done; a CI/CD pipeline is the automated part: CI builds and tests each commit, CD packages and releases it.
concepts.detection_hint: Pipeline-as-code files: .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, azure-pipelines.yml; issue-tracker statuses capture the human workflow.
concepts.example: GitHub Actions: checkout -> install -> lint -> test -> build -> deploy.

concepts.definition: A check is one automated verification run on a change (tests pass, lint clean, coverage threshold); a gate is a checkpoint that blocks progress until required checks pass.
concepts.detection_hint: Branch-protection rules via API; required-status-check lists; a failing check plus blocking gate is the enforcement point for every rule.
concepts.example: GitHub branch protection: require status checks and one approval before merge.

concepts.definition: A review is a human (or AI) examining a change before it merges, commenting on correctness, style, and design; an approval is the formal verdict that it may merge.
concepts.detection_hint: PR metadata: reviewers, review states, comment threads; mining review comments discovers unstated conventions (gold for a Chameleon-style tool).
concepts.example: GitHub PR review with Approve / Request changes; two-approval rule for payments code.

concepts.definition: The rule for how an approved branch's commits land in the main branch: merge commit (keep history), squash (collapse to one commit), or rebase (replay linearly).
concepts.detection_hint: Repo settings enforce allowed strategies; commit-graph shape after merges reveals which strategy a team actually uses.
concepts.example: GitHub's three buttons: Create a merge commit / Squash and merge / Rebase and merge.

concepts.definition: The version-numbering convention MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: bump MAJOR for breaking changes, MINOR for backward-compatible features, PATCH for backward-compatible fixes.
concepts.detection_hint: version fields in manifests; tools (semantic-release, changesets) derive the next version from commit messages and API diffs.
concepts.example: 2.4.1 -> 3.0.0 warns something will break; React 18.2.0 -> 18.3.0 added features safely.

concepts.definition: The human-readable, dated record of what changed in each released version; the bridge between version numbers and meaning.

concepts.definition: Logical container preventing name collisions.
concepts.detection_hint: namespace decl node wrapping decls

concepts.definition: Distributable unit of modules with manifest.

concepts.detection_hint: WithStmt node; using statement; AutoCloseable in try header
