concepts.definition: Collection-like abstraction mediating between domain and data-mapping layers.
concepts.detection_hint: Classes named *Repository/*Repo exposing find/save/add/remove; interface + DB-backed implementation pair; ORM access confined to them.
concepts.example: UserRepository.findByEmail(email) implemented over SQLAlchemy.

concepts.definition: Tracks changes across objects in a business transaction and commits them atomically.
concepts.detection_hint: commit()/rollback()/flush() lifecycle object shared across repositories; ORM Session/DbContext usage; transaction boundary wrappers.
concepts.example: with uow: repo.add(order); uow.commit()

concepts.definition: Composable named business-rule predicates combined with and/or/not.
concepts.detection_hint: Small predicate classes with isSatisfiedBy() plus and()/or()/not() combinators; names like *Specification/*Policy.
concepts.example: IsPremiumCustomer().and(HasOpenOrders()).isSatisfiedBy(user)

concepts.definition: Declarative query description object translated into storage queries.
concepts.detection_hint: Query-builder chains (where().orderBy().limit()) or dict/struct query objects passed to repositories.
concepts.example: criteria.where('age', '>', 18).orderBy('name')

concepts.definition: Separate layer moving data between in-memory objects and the database while keeping them independent.
concepts.detection_hint: Mapping config/annotations; toEntity()/fromEntity() converters; domain model free of persistence annotations.
concepts.example: SQLAlchemy mapper config keeping Order domain class persistence-free.

concepts.definition: Domain objects carrying their own persistence methods (save/find/delete).
concepts.detection_hint: Model classes inheriting a base Model with save()/find(); DB columns declared on the domain class; Rails/Django style.
concepts.example: user.save(); User.objects.filter(active=True)

concepts.definition: Ensures each database row maps to exactly one in-memory object per session.
concepts.detection_hint: Session/mapper cache keyed by primary key consulted before querying; get_by_id checks dict first.
concepts.example: ORM session returning the same object instance for repeated get(42).

concepts.definition: Data loaded only on first access rather than upfront.
concepts.detection_hint: Getter/proxy triggering fetch on first read; lazy=True flags; deferred imports; __getattr__ fetch logic.
concepts.example: ORM relationship proxy querying orders only when user.orders is touched.

concepts.definition: Central registry returning services on demand; contested because it hides dependencies.
concepts.detection_hint: Static Container.get(X)/locate() calls scattered in business code instead of injected constructor params; global registry singleton.
concepts.example: Container.resolve(EmailService) deep inside a method — flag hidden dependency.

concepts.definition: Do-nothing implementation of an interface returned instead of null.
concepts.detection_hint: Class named Null*/Noop* implementing the interface with empty method bodies; default no-op lambdas; removes repeated null checks.
concepts.example: NullLogger with empty log() assigned when no logger configured.

concepts.definition: Caching function results keyed by arguments to avoid recomputation.
concepts.detection_hint: lru_cache/functools.cache decorators; memoize wrappers; dict lookup on entry keyed by args; useMemo/computed.
concepts.example: @lru_cache def fib(n)

concepts.definition: Reusing expensive objects (connections, threads) from a managed pool.
concepts.detection_hint: acquire()/release()/get()/put() APIs; Pool classes with max-size config; connection-pool settings.
concepts.example: ConnectionPool(max=10).acquire() around DB access.

concepts.definition: Map of named prototype objects cloned on demand.
concepts.detection_hint: Dict of archetype instances plus clone(name)/spawn(name); template-entity copying.
concepts.example: enemyRegistry.clone('goblin') in a game.

concepts.definition: Encapsulating private state via closure/IIFE exposing a public API.
concepts.detection_hint: IIFE returning an object literal; ES modules with non-exported internals; _private naming conventions.
concepts.example: const counter = (() => { let n=0; return { inc: () => ++n } })()

concepts.definition: Module pattern variant defining members privately then revealing selected ones in the return object.
concepts.detection_hint: Return { pub: privateFn } mapping block at end of a closure/module.
concepts.example: return { start: _start, stop: _stop } at the end of an IIFE.

concepts.term: Observer vs Pub/Sub vs EventEmitter vs Signals
concepts.definition: Observer: subject keeps direct observer list. Pub/Sub: broker/topic decouples parties. EventEmitter: in-process named-event pub/sub. Signals: fine-grained reactive cells auto-tracking dependents.
concepts.detection_hint: attach/detach/notify (observer); broker publish/subscribe(topic) (pub/sub); on/off/emit (emitter); signal()/computed()/effect() reactive refs (signals).
concepts.example: emitter.on('save', fn); const count = signal(0); effect(() => render(count.value))

concepts.definition: Request flows through a linear pipeline of handlers that transform a context and may short-circuit.
concepts.detection_hint: use(fn) registration; (req, res, next) signatures; next() invocation; pipeline composition in web frameworks.
concepts.example: app.use(auth); app.use(logger); Express/Django middleware stacks.

concepts.definition: AOP-style hooks invoked before/after method calls or requests.
concepts.detection_hint: Interceptor registration; @Around aspects; client interceptors wrapping calls; request/response transform hooks.
concepts.example: HTTP client interceptor adding auth headers and retry logic.

concepts.definition: CoR: one of dynamically linked handlers handles the request. Middleware: all handlers may transform and pass a shared context.
concepts.detection_hint: setNext() links + early return = CoR; shared next() invocation mutating a context = middleware.
concepts.example: CoR: expense approval chain. Middleware: Express pipeline.

concepts.definition: Single dispatch entry routing command objects to their handlers (CQRS write side).
concepts.detection_hint: bus.dispatch(command) + handler registry keyed by command type; *Command/*Handler class pairs; handlers return void/Result.
concepts.example: commandBus.dispatch(new CreateOrder(...)) -> CreateOrderHandler.

concepts.definition: Dispatch pattern for read-side queries returning read models (CQRS read side).
concepts.detection_hint: bus.ask(query) + *Query/*QueryHandler pairs returning DTOs; no mutation in handlers.
concepts.example: queryBus.ask(new GetOrderSummary(id)) -> OrderSummaryDTO.

concepts.definition: Operations return a success/error wrapper instead of throwing.
concepts.detection_hint: Result<T>/Ok/Err types; isOk()/unwrap(); discriminated { ok, value } | { ok, error }; Go (T, error) returns.
concepts.example: function parse(s): Result<Date, ParseError>.

concepts.definition: Errors propagated as values through map/flatMap/bind chains (Either, Option, Result).
concepts.detection_hint: .map/.flatMap/.and_then chains on wrapper types; absence of throw in favor of returned errors; Rust ? operator.
concepts.example: fetchUser(id).flatMap(validate).map(toDTO)

concepts.definition: Chained configuration methods returning this for readable object construction.
concepts.detection_hint: High ratio of methods returning self/this; chained call sites; build()/exec() terminal method.
concepts.example: Query.select('a').from('t').where('x=1').build()

concepts.term: Facade vs Gateway vs Adapter vs Proxy
concepts.definition: Facade simplifies a subsystem; Gateway isolates an external system; Adapter converts an interface; Proxy controls access behind the same interface.
concepts.detection_hint: Facade delegates to many subsystem classes; Gateway wraps HTTP/RPC client behind an interface; Adapter translates signatures between two types; Proxy holds same-interface reference adding control.
concepts.example: StripeGateway wrapping SDK; ImageProxy lazy-loading; LegacyAdapter translating APIs.

concepts.definition: Horizontal layers (presentation, application, domain, infrastructure) each depending only downward.
concepts.detection_hint: Top-level dirs named presentation/application/domain/infrastructure or ui/service/dao; import graph shows strictly downward edges.
concepts.example: Classic Spring monolith with controllers -> services -> repositories.

concepts.definition: Model (data), View (UI), Controller (mediator); view observes model.
concepts.detection_hint: controllers/, models/, views/ directories; route -> controller#action mapping; controller classes handling HTTP verbs and rendering templates.
concepts.example: Rails/Django/Spring MVC apps.

concepts.definition: Passive View; Presenter holds presentation logic and updates the view through an interface.
concepts.detection_hint: *Presenter classes paired with view interfaces; view classes are dumb; presenter has no UI-framework imports.
concepts.example: Android Activities implementing view interfaces driven by Presenters.

concepts.definition: ViewModel exposes bindable state and commands; View data-binds to it.
concepts.detection_hint: *ViewModel classes with observable properties; two-way binding markup; ViewModels free of view imports.
concepts.example: WPF/Angular/Vue/SwiftUI screens with bound ViewModels.

concepts.definition: Unidirectional flow: Intent -> Model (reducer) -> View with immutable state.
concepts.detection_hint: Intent/State/Reducer/Effect type triads per screen; single immutable state object; intent sealed classes.
concepts.example: Kotlin Android screen: LoginIntent -> LoginReducer -> LoginState.

concepts.definition: Model-Update-View loop with pure update(msg, model) returning model and commands.
concepts.detection_hint: Model/Msg/update/view quartet per module; one Msg discriminated union; no side effects outside Cmd.
concepts.example: Elm/Fable/Bubble Tea programs.

concepts.definition: Actions dispatched to a store whose pure reducers produce new state triggering re-render.
concepts.detection_hint: actions/, reducers/, store, dispatch; pure (state, action) => state functions; action type constants.
concepts.example: Redux/React app with store.dispatch({type: 'ADD_TODO'}).

concepts.definition: Concentric rings (entities, use cases, adapters, frameworks) with dependencies pointing inward.
concepts.detection_hint: entities/, usecases/, adapters/, frameworks/ rings; domain ring has zero framework imports; interactor classes.
concepts.example: Uncle Bob's Clean Architecture layout.

concepts.definition: Core application exposes ports; external world connects via adapters.
concepts.detection_hint: ports/ interfaces + adapters/in|out/; driven vs driving split; core never imports adapter modules.
concepts.example: OrderPort implemented by PostgresOrderAdapter and RestOrderController.

concepts.definition: Domain model at the center, then domain services, application services, interfaces outward.
concepts.detection_hint: Domain.Model, Domain.Services, Application.Services, Infrastructure layers; inner layers reference nothing outward; composition root wires DI.
concepts.example: Jeffrey Palermo-style onion solution layout.

concepts.definition: Top-level structure names the domain, not the framework.
concepts.detection_hint: Top-level dirs named after business capabilities (billing/, shipping/) rather than controllers/; framework code nested inside domain dirs.
concepts.example: Repo root listing invoicing/, catalog/, accounts/ instead of src/controllers.

concepts.definition: Organize code by feature end-to-end (UI to DB) rather than by technical layer.
concepts.detection_hint: One self-contained folder per feature holding handler+view+model; cross-feature imports rare.
concepts.example: features/CreateOrder/ containing its handler, validator, and view.

concepts.definition: Single deployable split into modules with enforced boundaries and internal APIs.
concepts.detection_hint: Module dirs with public api/ and private internal/; per-module DB schemas; lint rules restricting cross-module imports.
concepts.example: Shop monolith with modules catalog/orders/payments each owning a schema.

concepts.definition: Independently deployable services owning their data and communicating over the network.
concepts.detection_hint: Separate deployable units (own Dockerfile/CI); own DB per service; no shared database; HTTP/gRPC clients between services; API contracts.
concepts.example: Checkout, payments, and shipping services with per-service databases.

concepts.definition: Coarse-grained services integrated via contracts over an enterprise service bus.
concepts.detection_hint: WSDL/SOAP artifacts; ESB configuration; service registries; contract-first schema files.
concepts.example: Enterprise SOA with ESB orchestrating SOAP services.

concepts.definition: Components react to events asynchronously via a broker.
concepts.detection_hint: events/ definitions; publish/emit calls and @EventListener handlers; broker (Kafka/RabbitMQ) config; topics.
concepts.example: OrderCreated events consumed by inventory and notification services.

concepts.definition: State derived by folding an immutable event log; events are the source of truth.
concepts.detection_hint: Event store tables/streams; apply(event) methods; aggregates rebuilt by folding; append-only storage; past-tense event names.
concepts.example: Account balance rebuilt from Deposited/Withdrawn events.

concepts.definition: Separate write model (commands) from read model (queries), often with separate stores.
concepts.detection_hint: commands/ + queries/ dirs; *CommandHandler/*QueryHandler; read-model projections; command handlers return void/Result, never data.
concepts.example: Command side writes normalized model; query side serves denormalized views.

concepts.definition: Distributed transaction as a sequence of local transactions with compensating actions.
concepts.detection_hint: *Saga/orchestrator classes; each step paired with compensateX; persisted saga state between steps.
concepts.example: BookTrip saga: BookFlight -> BookHotel, with CancelFlight on failure.

concepts.definition: Central coordinator commands workflow participants in sequence.
concepts.detection_hint: Central workflow/orchestrator file calling services in sequence; state machine persisted; step sequencing explicit.
concepts.example: OrderOrchestrator calling payment then inventory then shipping.

concepts.definition: Workflow participants react to events peer-to-peer with no central coordinator.
concepts.detection_hint: Handlers only reacting to events and emitting follow-up events; no central sequencer file.
concepts.example: Payment service emits PaymentCompleted; inventory listens and reserves.

concepts.definition: Producers publish to topics; a broker delivers to all subscribers.
concepts.detection_hint: Topic definitions; subscribe consumers; no direct import between publisher and subscriber modules.
concepts.example: Google Pub/Sub or SNS topics feeding multiple subscriber services.

concepts.definition: Point-to-point async task delivery with competing consumers.
concepts.detection_hint: Queue producers and worker/consumer processes; ack/retry/DLQ config; job payload structs.
concepts.example: Sidekiq/Celery/RabbitMQ workers processing email jobs.

concepts.definition: Processing as a chain of independent transformations connected by streams.
concepts.detection_hint: Chained map/filter/reduce or | pipelines; stream APIs; components reading input and emitting output with no shared state.
concepts.example: Unix pipelines; compiler passes; log processing chains.

concepts.definition: Shared knowledge base refined opportunistically by independent specialist components.
concepts.detection_hint: Central shared data store with multiple worker modules reading/writing partial results.
concepts.example: Speech-recognition systems with specialist solvers refining hypotheses.

concepts.definition: Intermediary coordinating communication between decoupled distributed components.
concepts.detection_hint: Broker/proxy/stub generated code; registry lookups; clients never hold direct server references.
concepts.example: CORBA ORB; message brokers decoupling senders and receivers.

concepts.definition: Nodes acting as both client and server without central authority.
concepts.detection_hint: DHT code; peer discovery; symmetric node logic; same binary serving and making requests.
concepts.example: BitTorrent clients; blockchain nodes.

concepts.definition: Centralized server providing resources to requesting clients.
concepts.detection_hint: Separate client/ and server/ deployables; HTTP/RPC client stubs; server listening on sockets.
concepts.example: React SPA consuming a REST API server.

concepts.definition: Stateless functions triggered by events with platform-managed scaling.
concepts.detection_hint: handler(event, context) entry points; serverless.yml/SAM templates; trigger bindings; no long-lived server process.
concepts.example: AWS Lambda functions per endpoint behind API Gateway.

concepts.definition: Dedicated backend per client type aggregating downstream APIs into client-shaped payloads.
concepts.detection_hint: bff-web/, bff-mobile/ services calling common downstream APIs; thin aggregation with client-specific DTO shaping.
concepts.example: Mobile BFF aggregating profile+orders+recommendations in one call.

concepts.definition: Single entry point routing, authenticating, and rate-limiting requests to internal services.
concepts.detection_hint: Route table config; gateway service (Kong/Envoy/NGINX); auth middleware centralized; all external traffic funnels through one config.
concepts.example: Kong gateway routing /users and /orders to internal services.

concepts.definition: Helper container co-deployed with the app for cross-cutting concerns (proxy, logging, config).
concepts.detection_hint: Two containers per pod spec; istio-proxy/envoy; shared volumes or network namespace between app and helper.
concepts.example: Envoy sidecar handling mTLS and metrics for the app container.

concepts.definition: Local proxy sidecar brokering outbound connections for the application.
concepts.detection_hint: App config pointing at localhost for remote services; local proxy configuration.
concepts.example: App connecting to localhost:5432 proxied by an ambassador to a remote DB.

concepts.definition: Gradually replacing a legacy system by routing functionality to new services at the boundary.
concepts.detection_hint: Routing rules splitting traffic old vs new; facade/proxy in front of legacy; incremental route migration.
concepts.example: Gateway routing /orders to the new service while everything else hits the legacy monolith.

concepts.definition: Translation layer protecting a clean domain model from a legacy/external model's concepts.
concepts.detection_hint: acl/ or translation/ adapters at the boundary; external DTOs converted to domain types; no external types leak past the layer.
concepts.example: LegacyCustomerTranslator mapping SOAP types into domain Customer.

concepts.definition: Fail fast when a dependency is unhealthy; open/half-open/closed state machine around calls.
concepts.detection_hint: CircuitBreaker wrappers; failure-threshold/reset config; fallback functions adjacent to call sites.
concepts.example: Resilience4j breaker falling back to cached prices when the pricing service fails.

concepts.definition: Isolate resources (thread pools, connections) per dependency so one failure cannot sink everything.
concepts.detection_hint: Separate pools/clients per downstream service; per-dependency executor config; isolation boundaries.
concepts.example: Dedicated connection pool for payments vs one for recommendations.

concepts.definition: Re-attempt failed operations with increasing delays and jitter.
concepts.detection_hint: @Retryable annotations; retry policies (maxAttempts, backoff, jitter); exponential sleep formulas; retry decorators around network calls.
concepts.example: retry(stop=3, wait=exponential+jitter) on an HTTP call.

concepts.definition: Save domain event in the same DB transaction as state; a relay publishes it reliably.
concepts.detection_hint: outbox table; event insert adjacent to entity save; background poller/CDC relay publishing.
concepts.example: OrderCreated row written with the order, Debezium relays to Kafka.

concepts.definition: Record processed message IDs so redelivery is safe.
concepts.detection_hint: processed_messages/inbox table; dedup check on messageId at consumer start; unique constraint on message ID.
concepts.example: Consumer inserts messageId first; duplicate delivery becomes a no-op.

concepts.definition: Horizontal data partition across nodes by shard key.
concepts.detection_hint: Shard-key routing logic; per-shard connection config; router choosing DB by hash/key range of ID.
concepts.example: Users A-M on db1, N-Z on db2; consistent-hash routing.

concepts.definition: Writes go to the primary; reads served by replicas.
concepts.detection_hint: Separate read/write connection pools or DSNs; readDb/writeDb clients; SELECT routed to replica pool.
concepts.example: Django DATABASE_ROUTERS sending reads to replicas.

concepts.definition: Denormalized projections optimized for specific queries, fed by events.
concepts.detection_hint: projections/ modules; denormalized table per view; project(event) handlers; rebuild-from-events scripts.
concepts.example: OrderSummary projection updated by OrderCreated/ItemAdded events.

concepts.definition: UI expresses user intents (commands) rather than CRUD forms over raw entities.
concepts.detection_hint: Endpoints/commands named with domain verbs (DeactivateUser, MoveOrder) instead of entity CRUD routes; intent-shaped DTOs.
concepts.example: POST /orders/{id}/cancel instead of PUT /orders/{id} with status field.

concepts.definition: A class should have only one reason to change — one actor.
concepts.detection_hint: Class touching multiple unrelated subsystems (DB + SMTP + UI imports); many unrelated public methods; low cohesion (high LCOM).
concepts.example: User class that validates, persists, and emails — split into User, UserRepository, UserMailer.

concepts.definition: Open for extension, closed for modification: add behavior via new code, not edits.
concepts.detection_hint: Switch/if-chains on type edited per new feature; instanceof/typeof chains; recurring multi-branch conditionals on one discriminant.
concepts.example: Adding a new shape requires editing every area() switch — use polymorphic Shape.area().

concepts.definition: Subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.
concepts.detection_hint: Overrides throwing NotSupportedException; empty overrides; isinstance checks before calling base API; strengthened preconditions.
concepts.example: Square extends Rectangle breaking setWidth/setHeight invariants.

concepts.definition: Many client-specific interfaces beat one fat general-purpose interface.
concepts.detection_hint: Interfaces with many methods where implementers stub most; empty method bodies in implementations; clients using only a subset.
concepts.example: IWorker with work()/eat()/sleep() forcing Robot to stub eat().

concepts.definition: High-level modules depend on abstractions, not concrete low-level modules.
concepts.detection_hint: new of concrete infrastructure inside business logic; domain layer importing infra packages; constructor params typed as concrete classes.
concepts.example: OrderService constructing MySqlRepository internally instead of accepting a Repository interface.

concepts.definition: Every piece of knowledge has a single authoritative representation.
concepts.detection_hint: Duplicate code blocks via token-similarity/hash clone detection (>=6 identical lines); copy-pasted logic with renamed identifiers.
concepts.example: Same validation block copied into four controllers.

concepts.definition: Prefer the simplest design that works.
concepts.detection_hint: Excessive cyclomatic complexity for the task; deep nesting; abstraction layers with a single perpetual implementation.
concepts.example: Recursive regex parser where a split() suffices.

concepts.definition: Do not build capability before it is needed.
concepts.detection_hint: Unused parameters/options; dead public APIs; extension hooks with zero callers; 'for future use' TODOs.
concepts.example: Plugin system with one plugin ever written, adding three abstraction layers.

concepts.definition: Deliberate tolerance of small duplication: prefer duplication over the wrong abstraction.
concepts.detection_hint: Weigh duplication findings against coupling introduced by deduplication; flag premature shared abstractions (high fan-in to unstable modules).
concepts.example: Two similar-but-evolving report functions kept separate until their shape stabilizes.

concepts.definition: Distinct concerns (UI, logic, persistence) live in distinct modules.
concepts.detection_hint: Single module importing UI framework + DB driver + business rules together.
concepts.example: A view file issuing SQL queries directly.

concepts.definition: All statements in a function operate at one abstraction level.
concepts.detection_hint: Function mixing low-level string/byte manipulation with high-level domain calls.
concepts.example: processOrder() interleaving checksum math with shipping workflow calls.

concepts.definition: Build behavior by composing objects rather than subclassing.
concepts.detection_hint: Inheritance depth > 3; subclasses overriding most inherited members; has-a alternatives available.
concepts.example: Duck extends Bird overriding fly() to throw — compose a FlightBehavior instead.

concepts.definition: Isolate likely change behind a stable interface.
concepts.detection_hint: Scattered conditionals on the same variable co-changing across commits; variation hardcoded in many places.
concepts.example: Tax rules embedded in 12 places vs a TaxPolicy module.

concepts.definition: Depend on contracts, not concrete classes.
concepts.detection_hint: Signatures typed with concrete classes where interfaces exist; low ratio of interfaces/protocols in codebase.
concepts.example: def process(repo: PostgresRepo) instead of def process(repo: Repository).

concepts.definition: A unit should only call its immediate collaborators, not reach through object graphs.
concepts.detection_hint: Call chains a.getB().getC().doX() with >2 hops; train-wreck expressions; message-chain counts.
concepts.example: order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZip() — ask order for the zip.

concepts.definition: Behavior should match what users and readers expect.
concepts.detection_hint: Getters that mutate; side effects in equals/hash; names contradicting behavior.
concepts.example: getTotal() that also recalculates and persists the total.

concepts.definition: Report errors immediately at the source rather than propagating corrupt state.
concepts.detection_hint: Missing argument validation at public entry points; swallowed exceptions (empty catch); nulls passed deep into the system.
concepts.example: Assert non-null orderId at the API boundary, not 10 calls deep.

concepts.definition: Anticipate and guard against misuse and invalid input everywhere.
concepts.detection_hint: Assertion/guard density at boundaries; input validation in public APIs; absence of validation at trust boundaries is the flag.
concepts.example: Validating untrusted request payloads before any processing.

concepts.definition: Crash loudly on internal invariant violations; defend only at trust boundaries.
concepts.detection_hint: Asserts on internal invariants; intentional unreachable/panic branches; no defensive null checks on internally-guaranteed values.
concepts.example: assert(items.length > 0) after a filter that guarantees it, then crash if wrong.

concepts.definition: Sensible defaults inferred from naming/structure; configure only deviations.
concepts.detection_hint: Framework-driven layout (Rails/Django-style); small config relative to codebase; naming-based auto-wiring.
concepts.example: UsersController auto-mapped to /users without route config.

concepts.definition: Behavior should be visible in code, not hidden in magic (Zen of Python).
concepts.detection_hint: Magic strings driving behavior; implicit globals; monkey-patching; metaprogramming hiding control flow.
concepts.example: require('./plugins') auto-registering handlers via side effects.

concepts.definition: Twelve practices for portable cloud apps: one codebase/many deploys; declared isolated deps; config in environment; backing services as attached resources; separated build/release/run; stateless processes; port binding; scale via processes; disposability; dev/prod parity; logs as event streams; admin tasks as one-off processes.
concepts.detection_hint: Hardcoded config/secrets (violates 3); undeclared vendored deps (2); file-based logging (11); shared mutable in-process state (6); missing healthcheck/fast-shutdown handling (9).
concepts.example: Env-var config, stdout logging, stateless web processes scaled horizontally.

concepts.definition: Assign responsibility to the class that has the information needed.
concepts.detection_hint: Methods placed far from the data they use; feature-envy metric identifying the true expert class.
concepts.example: Order computes its own total because it holds the line items.

concepts.definition: B creates A if B contains, aggregates, records, or has initialization data for A.
concepts.detection_hint: Objects created by unrelated strangers instead of their containers/aggregates.
concepts.example: Order creates OrderLine items, not the controller.

concepts.definition: Delegate UI events to a non-UI coordinator object.
concepts.detection_hint: Business logic inside event handlers/views; UI classes calling domain/persistence directly.
concepts.example: CheckoutController coordinating use cases instead of the button handler doing so.

concepts.definition: Minimize dependencies between classes.
concepts.detection_hint: High fan-out/efferent coupling metrics; large import counts per module.
concepts.example: Class importing 30 other classes across 8 packages.

concepts.definition: Keep related responsibilities together.
concepts.detection_hint: High LCOM (methods not sharing fields); utility grab-bag classes; unrelated method clusters.
concepts.example: Utils class with date math, string formatting, and HTTP helpers.

concepts.definition: Handle type-based variation via polymorphic operations, not conditionals.
concepts.detection_hint: Switch-on-type duplicated across the codebase (OCP signal).
concepts.example: Notification.send() per channel instead of if type == 'email'.

concepts.definition: Invent an artificial class for a responsibility belonging to no domain object.
concepts.detection_hint: Service/manager classes not mapping to domain nouns; confirm they raise cohesion and lower coupling.
concepts.example: Repository classes persisting domain objects.

concepts.definition: Introduce an intermediate to decouple components.
concepts.detection_hint: Adapters/mediators between subsystems; delegation layers; watch for middle-man overuse.
concepts.example: TaxCalculatorAdapter decoupling the app from a vendor tax API.

concepts.definition: Wrap points of likely variation behind stable interfaces.
concepts.detection_hint: Volatile modules lacking an interface boundary; instability metric combined with absence of abstractions.
concepts.example: Payment gateway hidden behind a PaymentProvider interface.

concepts.definition: The granule of reuse is the granule of release: packages versioned as coherent units.
concepts.detection_hint: Version/release tags vs package boundaries; consumers importing partial internals of a package.
concepts.example: Publishing internal classes forces semver bumps for internal changes.

concepts.definition: Classes used together are packaged together; don't force dependence on the unused.
concepts.detection_hint: Package-level fan-in analysis: consumers using only a fraction of a package's classes; fat dependency pulling transitives.
concepts.example: Importing a mega-utils package for one function.

concepts.definition: Classes that change together are packaged together.
concepts.detection_hint: Git co-change analysis: files always committed together living in different packages.
concepts.example: Every pricing change touching files in four different packages.

concepts.definition: No cycles in the package dependency graph.
concepts.detection_hint: Cycle detection (strongly connected components) on the module import graph.
concepts.example: package A imports B which imports A — extract a shared abstraction.

concepts.definition: Depend in the direction of stability.
concepts.detection_hint: Instability metric I = Ce/(Ca+Ce); flag stable packages depending on volatile ones.
concepts.example: Core domain depending on a churn-heavy experimental module.

concepts.definition: Stable packages should be abstract; instability belongs in concretions.
concepts.detection_hint: Abstract-type ratio per package vs instability; distance from main sequence D = |A + I - 1|.
concepts.example: A heavily depended-on package full of concrete god classes.

concepts.definition: SOLID reinterpreted functionally: one transformation per function; extend via composition; honor contracts; small signatures; inject behavior via higher-order params.
concepts.detection_hint: Function-granularity metrics: large param lists, switch dispatch instead of injected functions, functions calling concrete helpers instead of passed-in behavior.
concepts.example: process(data, validate, transform, persist) with behaviors injected.

concepts.definition: Do one thing well; programs work together; handle text streams.
concepts.detection_hint: Tools with single clear purpose and composable I/O; flag monolithic multi-mode binaries with sprawling flags.
concepts.example: grep | sort | uniq -c composition.

concepts.definition: Simplicity of implementation beats completeness/consistency ideals for adoption (Gabriel).
concepts.detection_hint: Contextual principle for design tradeoff analysis; not directly measurable — informs severity weighting of complexity findings.
concepts.example: C and Unix spreading despite MIT-style 'right thing' alternatives.

concepts.definition: Be conservative in what you send, liberal in what you accept.
concepts.detection_hint: Strict output validation and lenient input parsing (or absence of either); over-liberality conflicts with fail fast.
concepts.example: API accepting both 'true' and true but emitting strictly typed JSON.

concepts.definition: With enough users, every observable behavior of an API becomes a depended-upon contract.
concepts.detection_hint: Contextual: informs versioning/deprecation policy checks; flag changes to undocumented-but-observable behavior.
concepts.example: Clients depending on error-message text or response ordering.

concepts.definition: Systems mirror the communication structures of the organizations building them.
concepts.detection_hint: Module ownership vs contribution analysis: module touched mostly by a team that does not own it; repo boundaries misaligned with teams.
concepts.example: Four teams producing a four-tier system with matching seams.

concepts.definition: Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later.
concepts.detection_hint: Contextual process principle; not code-detectable.
concepts.example: Mythical Man-Month staffing escalation.

concepts.definition: A distributed store guarantees at most two of Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance; with partitions mandatory, choose CP or AP.
concepts.detection_hint: Datastore config revealing the choice: quorum/consistency-level settings, replication factor, linearizable flags.
concepts.example: Cassandra QUORUM reads (CP-leaning) vs ANY (AP-leaning).

concepts.definition: Transactions guarantee Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.
concepts.detection_hint: Transaction usage (BEGIN/COMMIT), isolation-level settings, ORM transaction scopes; absence of transactions around multi-write flows is a flag.
concepts.example: BEGIN; debit; credit; COMMIT around a funds transfer.

concepts.definition: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventually consistent — the NoSQL availability-first model.
concepts.detection_hint: Eventual-consistency configs; saga/compensation code; conflict-resolution/merge logic; tunable consistency levels.
concepts.example: Dynamo-style store with last-write-wins and read repair.

concepts.definition: Eight false assumptions: network reliable; latency zero; bandwidth infinite; network secure; topology fixed; one administrator; transport cost zero; network homogeneous.
concepts.detection_hint: Remote calls without timeouts/retries (1-3); unauthenticated internal RPCs (4); hardcoded hosts (5); chatty fine-grained remote APIs (2,7).
concepts.example: HTTP client with no timeout calling a payment service.

concepts.definition: Roughly 80% of effects come from 20% of causes; optimize the hot fraction.
concepts.detection_hint: Concentration metrics: 20% of modules holding 80% of churn/defects/profiling time.
concepts.example: Profiling shows 3 functions consuming 78% of CPU.

concepts.definition: Leave the code cleaner than you found it.
concepts.detection_hint: Per-commit complexity trend: cognitive complexity or lint-warning delta per diff should trend non-positive.
concepts.example: Each PR slightly reduces warnings in files it touches.

concepts.definition: Visible disorder invites more disorder; fix small degradations early.
concepts.detection_hint: Correlation between lint-warning density and defect density; TODO/FIXME accumulation rate.
concepts.example: File with 200 suppressed warnings accrues bugs at 3x rate.

concepts.definition: Copying patterns or code without understanding why they exist.
concepts.detection_hint: Verbatim boilerplate with no functional role: unused config blocks, ritual interfaces with a single implementation and no variation, copied ceremony.
concepts.example: Every service has an empty ApplicationEventPublisher wire-up copied from a tutorial.

concepts.definition: Over-applying one familiar tool or pattern to every problem.
concepts.detection_hint: Same pattern/framework applied across inappropriate domains; regex parsing nested structures; singletons everywhere; one framework for all problems regardless of fit.
concepts.example: Using Kafka for a two-service request/response flow that needs synchronous calls.

concepts.definition: Choosing technologies for CV appeal rather than fit (wink, but real).
concepts.detection_hint: Polyglot sprawl: many languages/frameworks each powering a single tiny component; trendy dependencies with minimal usage.
concepts.example: Five microservices in five languages sharing one Postgres database.

concepts.definition: A method doing too much; hard to name, reuse, or test (Bloater).
concepts.detection_hint: Method > 30-50 lines; cyclomatic complexity > 10; many local variables; nesting depth > 3.
concepts.example: 150-line handleRequest() doing parsing, validation, business logic, and rendering.

concepts.definition: A class with too many responsibilities and fields (Bloater).
concepts.detection_hint: Class > 500 lines; > 20 methods; > 10 fields; high WMC; low LCOM cohesion.
concepts.example: God class Manager coordinating every subsystem.

concepts.definition: Using primitives instead of small domain objects (Bloater).
concepts.detection_hint: High ratio of primitive-typed params/fields; same string/int validated repeatedly; related primitives traveling together.
concepts.example: Money as float and currency as string instead of a Money value object.

concepts.definition: More parameters than a reader can hold in mind (Bloater).
concepts.detection_hint: Function with > 3-5 parameters; many boolean flag parameters.
concepts.example: createUser(name, email, age, street, city, zip, country, isAdmin).

concepts.definition: The same variable group traveling together across signatures (Bloater).
concepts.detection_hint: Same set of >= 3 fields/params recurring in >= 3 signatures/structs; suggest parameter/value object.
concepts.example: street/city/zip passed to five functions — extract Address.

concepts.definition: The same switch/if-else on a type code duplicated across the codebase (OO abuser).
concepts.detection_hint: switch/match/instanceof on the same discriminant in > 1 place; adding a type requires multi-file edits.
concepts.example: switch(shape.type) in area(), draw(), and serialize().

concepts.definition: Field set only in some circumstances, invalid otherwise (OO abuser).
concepts.detection_hint: Fields written in one method only; fields read under the same condition they are set; high percentage of nullable instance fields.
concepts.example: taxRate field only meaningful during calculate() call sequence.

concepts.definition: Subclass inherits but rejects much of the parent's interface (OO abuser).
concepts.detection_hint: Subclass overriding methods with empty/throw bodies; subclass using < 30% of inherited members.
concepts.example: Stack extends Vector overriding add() to throw.

concepts.definition: Two classes doing the same job with different method names (OO abuser).
concepts.detection_hint: Similar method bodies across classes with different names (clone detection); parallel public method sets.
concepts.example: JsonWriter.write() vs XmlSerializer.emit() doing identical traversal.

concepts.definition: Every subclass of hierarchy A forces a matching subclass of B (OO abuser).
concepts.detection_hint: Two class trees whose leaf names mirror each other; parallel co-change in git history.
concepts.example: Adding XWriter requires adding XReader in a mirrored tree.

concepts.definition: One class routinely changed for many different reasons (change preventer).
concepts.detection_hint: Git co-change: one file modified in many unrelated commit topics; class importing unrelated subsystems; SRP metrics.
concepts.example: User class edited for auth, billing, and UI changes alike.

concepts.definition: One conceptual change forces edits in many classes (change preventer).
concepts.detection_hint: Git co-change: many files always committed together; fan-out from one constant/type to many modules.
concepts.example: Adding a field requires touching DTO, mapper, validator, view, and tests in five modules.

concepts.definition: Comments explaining what the code should say itself (dispensable); why-comments are fine.
concepts.detection_hint: Comment-to-code ratio spikes inside long methods; comments restating identifiers; commented-out code blocks.
concepts.example: // increment i above i += 1; stale block of disabled code.

concepts.definition: Same code in multiple places (dispensable).
concepts.detection_hint: Exact clones (>= 6 identical lines / >= 50 tokens) and near-miss clones (token similarity > 80% with renames).
concepts.example: Same normalization logic copied across three API handlers.

concepts.definition: A class not doing enough to justify its existence (dispensable).
concepts.detection_hint: Class with <= 2 trivial methods, tiny field count, only delegates; single-use single-impl interfaces.
concepts.example: NameHelper class with one formatName() method used once.

concepts.definition: Dumb field holders with accessors and no behavior (dispensable).
concepts.detection_hint: Getter/setter-only classes; zero methods referencing own fields beyond accessors; pair with Feature Envy findings on clients.
concepts.example: CustomerDTO with 20 getters/setters and no logic.

concepts.definition: Code never executed (dispensable).
concepts.detection_hint: Unreachable statements after return/throw; private methods with zero call sites; exported symbols with zero importers; coverage = 0.
concepts.example: legacyExport() unreferenced since the v1 API shutdown.

concepts.definition: Abstractions built for the future with one or no real use (dispensable).
concepts.detection_hint: Abstract classes/interfaces with exactly one implementer and no tests; unused generic parameters; hooks never exercised.
concepts.example: AbstractStrategyBase with a single concrete subclass for three years.

concepts.definition: A method uses another object's data more than its own (coupler).
concepts.detection_hint: Per-method ratio of external-class accesses to own-class accesses > 1; identifies the envied target class.
concepts.example: total() in Report reaches into Order fields nine times, its own once.

concepts.definition: Two classes poking at each other's internals (coupler).
concepts.detection_hint: Bidirectional dependencies between class pairs; mutual field access counts; friend/internal access frequency.
concepts.example: Order and Invoice each reading the other's private fields.

concepts.definition: Client navigates the whole object graph via chained calls (coupler).
concepts.detection_hint: Call-chain length > 2-3; Law of Demeter violation count; chains touching > 2 distinct types.
concepts.example: a.getB().getC().getD().compute() at call sites.

concepts.definition: A class that only delegates to another (coupler).
concepts.detection_hint: Fraction of methods that are pure delegation > 50-70%; no added logic.
concepts.example: Facade-like wrapper forwarding 12 of 13 methods unchanged.

concepts.definition: Library type lacks a needed method so workarounds accumulate (coupler).
concepts.detection_hint: Helper/utility methods operating on a single foreign type clustered in random places; repeated extension-method workarounds.
concepts.example: DateUtils scattered across five modules wrapping the same library type.

concepts.definition: Move a code fragment into a new method named after its intent; inverse: Inline Method.
concepts.detection_hint: Tool: select duplicated/comment-worthy fragments in long methods and propose extraction with inferred params/returns; fully automatable.
concepts.example: Extract validateOrder() from a 100-line processOrder().

concepts.definition: Replace calls with the body when indirection adds nothing; inverse: Extract Method.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: single-call trivial delegating methods replaced by body at call sites.
concepts.example: Inline one-line getName() delegating to field.

concepts.definition: Assign a complex subexpression to a well-named temp; inverse: Inline Variable.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: detect repeated/complex subexpressions and propose named extraction.
concepts.example: const isEligible = age >= 18 && hasLicense && !suspended.

concepts.definition: Replace a single-assignment temp with its expression; inverse: Extract Variable.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: temps assigned once from a simple expression and read once.
concepts.example: Inline `const t = user.name` used once.

concepts.definition: Rename variable/function/class/file to match intent.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable with cross-file reference resolution and import updates.
concepts.example: Rename calc() to computeInvoiceTotal() repo-wide.

concepts.definition: Move a member to the class that uses it most.
concepts.detection_hint: Partial: tool proposes target via feature-envy/access analysis; human confirms semantics and updates references.
concepts.example: Move total() from Report into Order whose fields it reads.

concepts.definition: Split a coherent subset of fields+methods from a large class; inverse: Inline Class.
concepts.detection_hint: Partial: tool clusters fields/methods by usage cohesion (LCOM) and proposes the split.
concepts.example: Extract Address from Customer's street/city/zip cluster.

concepts.definition: Merge a lazy class back into its user; inverse: Extract Class.
concepts.detection_hint: Partial: tool detects lazy classes and moves members into the sole consumer.
concepts.example: Inline one-method NameHelper into UserProfile.

concepts.definition: Declare an interface from the subset of methods clients actually use.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: analyze client call sites to derive the used method set and emit the interface.
concepts.example: Extract Notifier { send() } from EmailService for test doubles.

concepts.definition: Move duplicated members from sibling subclasses to the superclass; inverse: Push Down.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: detect identical members across siblings and hoist.
concepts.example: Pull identical validate() from PdfReport/CsvReport into Report.

concepts.definition: Move a superclass member into the only subclasses using it; inverse: Pull Up.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: usage analysis shows member referenced by one/few subclasses.
concepts.example: Push commission() from Employee into Salesperson.

concepts.definition: Move each switch branch into an overriding method of a subtype.
concepts.detection_hint: Partial: tool rewrites dispatch and scaffolds subtypes; human designs hierarchy and names.
concepts.example: switch(bird.type).speed() becomes Bird subclasses with speed() overrides.

concepts.term: Replace Magic Number with Symbolic Constant
concepts.definition: Replace bare literals with named constants.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: detect repeated/semantically-loaded literals and hoist named constants.
concepts.example: if (status == 9) becomes if (status == SHIPPED).

concepts.definition: Bundle a traveling parameter group into an object.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: data-clump detection feeds parameter-object extraction and signature rewrite.
concepts.example: foo(street, city, zip) becomes foo(address).

concepts.term: Replace Nested Conditional with Guard Clauses
concepts.definition: Flatten nested ifs into early returns.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: restructure nesting depth > 3 into guard clauses preserving semantics.
concepts.example: if(!user) return; if(!user.active) return; ...

concepts.definition: Extract condition and each branch into intention-revealing methods.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: extract complex boolean expressions and branch bodies into named helpers.
concepts.example: if (date.isBefore(SUMMER_START) || ...) becomes if (isSummer(date)).

concepts.definition: Combine tests with the same result into one condition; inverse: Decompose Conditional.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: detect adjacent conditionals with identical bodies and merge with and/or.
concepts.example: if(a) return 0; if(b) return 0; becomes if (a || b) return 0.

concepts.definition: Replace a temp with a method computing it, unblocking Extract Method.
concepts.detection_hint: Partial: tool extracts the computation; side-effect analysis needed for safety.
concepts.example: Replace `basePrice = qty * price` temp with basePrice() query.

concepts.definition: Split a function doing two separable things into sequential phases with a data handoff.
concepts.detection_hint: Partial: tool identifies input-only vs dependent statement groups and proposes the split.
concepts.example: Split priceOrder into parseOrder(json) then computePrice(order).

concepts.definition: Make a public field private with accessor methods controlling invariants.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: generate accessors and rewrite direct accesses.
concepts.example: Public age field becomes private with setAge validating >= 0.

concepts.definition: Stop exposing internal collections; return copies/views and provide add/remove.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: detect getters returning mutable internal collections; rewrite to copy/readonly plus mutation methods.
concepts.example: getOrders() returns List.copyOf(orders); use addOrder().

concepts.definition: Use a named factory for creation needing caching, subtype selection, or validation.
concepts.detection_hint: Partial: tool rewrites call sites to factory; naming and caching policy are human decisions.
concepts.example: Color.fromHex('#fff') instead of new Color(...).

concepts.definition: Throw instead of returning ignorable error codes (and the reverse: Replace Exceptions with Error Code/Result).
concepts.detection_hint: Partial both directions: tool rewrites call sites; convention choice and boundary policy are human.
concepts.example: if (result == -1) handling becomes try/except or Result<T> returns.

concepts.definition: Add, remove, reorder, or rename parameters; rename the function.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable with cross-file reference resolution updating all call sites.
concepts.example: Drop unused legacy flag parameter from search() and update 40 call sites.

concepts.definition: Create a method on the server that hides navigation to its delegate; inverse: Remove Middle Man.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: message-chain detection proposes delegate-hiding methods.
concepts.example: person.department.manager.name becomes person.managerName().

concepts.definition: Remove pure-delegation layers so clients talk to the real object; inverse: Hide Delegate.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: middle-man detection (> 50-70% delegation) proposes inlining the delegate.
concepts.example: Delete wrapper forwarding 12 of 13 methods to repo.

concepts.definition: Replace an algorithm body with a clearer or simpler equivalent.
concepts.detection_hint: Not automatable: human rewrites; tool can flag complexity hotspots as candidates.
concepts.example: Replace hand-rolled sort loop with built-in timsort.

concepts.definition: Return a do-nothing object instead of null to remove repeated null checks.
concepts.detection_hint: Partial: tool finds repeated `if x is null` call-site clusters and scaffolds the Null class.
concepts.example: NullCustomer with empty methods removes 20 null guards.

concepts.definition: Split methods that both return a value and mutate state.
concepts.detection_hint: Partial: side-effect analysis flags getters that mutate; tool splits call sites.
concepts.example: getAndAdvance() becomes current() plus advance().

concepts.definition: Merge methods differing only in a literal/enum into one parameterized method.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: clone detection over sibling methods differing by constants.
concepts.example: fivePercentRaise()/tenPercentRaise() become raise(percent).

concepts.definition: Pass the whole object instead of pulling several fields out of it as args.
concepts.detection_hint: Automatable: detect args all sourced from one object at call sites; rewrite signature.
concepts.example: within(plan.low, plan.high) becomes within(plan).

concepts.definition: Test structure: set up state, execute one behavior, verify the outcome.
concepts.detection_hint: Test bodies segmentable into setup/call/assert regions; flag tests with multiple acts or scattered assert clusters.
concepts.example: arrange: new Cart(); act: cart.add(item); assert: cart.total == 10.

concepts.definition: BDD phrasing of AAA: context, event, outcome.
concepts.detection_hint: given/when/then or describe/it blocks; Gherkin .feature files.
concepts.example: Given a logged-in user, When they checkout, Then stock decreases.

concepts.definition: Many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests, very few E2E tests.
concepts.detection_hint: Ratio of unit : integration : e2e tests; flag inverted pyramids / ice-cream cones.
concepts.example: 800 unit, 80 integration, 8 e2e tests.

concepts.definition: Dummy: passed, never used. Fake: working simplified impl. Stub: canned answers. Spy: records calls. Mock: verifies expectations.
concepts.detection_hint: Classify doubles by whether assertions target the double (mock/spy) or the SUT output (stub/fake); dummy = unused param.
concepts.example: InMemoryRepo (fake); stubbed pricing API; mock mailer expecting send() once.

concepts.definition: Fixed baseline state/data a test runs against.
concepts.detection_hint: setUp/tearDown, beforeEach/afterEach, fixture files, conftest; flag shared mutable fixtures.
concepts.example: pytest fixture creating a seeded test database.

concepts.definition: Factories build fresh objects per test; fixtures are shared predefined state.
concepts.detection_hint: Object-mother/builder functions in tests vs shared data files; flag inter-test coupling through shared fixtures.
concepts.example: factory_boy UserFactory vs a shared users.json fixture.

concepts.definition: Generate many random inputs and assert invariants/properties hold.
concepts.detection_hint: forAll/@given/fc.assert constructs; generator/arbitrary definitions in tests.
concepts.example: forAll(list): reverse(reverse(list)) == list.

concepts.definition: Capture full output once and diff future runs against it.
concepts.detection_hint: __snapshots__, .snap/golden files; approval-test frameworks; flag snapshot churn without corresponding code change.
concepts.example: React component snapshot diffed on each render test.

concepts.definition: Mutate source and require tests to kill mutants; measures suite quality.
concepts.detection_hint: mutmut/Stryker/PIT config presence; mutation score metric; surviving mutants listed.
concepts.example: Stryker reports 82% mutation score with 12 surviving mutants.

concepts.definition: One test logic driven by a table of input/expected cases.
concepts.detection_hint: @parameterized/it.each/@pytest.mark.parametrize/table-driven test slices.

concepts.definition: Fixed set of worker threads consuming tasks from a queue.
concepts.detection_hint: ExecutorService/ThreadPoolExecutor/worker-pool config with size; absence of raw per-task thread spawning.
concepts.example: ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) handling requests.

concepts.definition: Producers enqueue work; consumers dequeue; the queue decouples their rates.
concepts.detection_hint: Blocking queue/channel shared between publisher loops and worker loops; ack/put/get patterns.
concepts.example: queue.Queue feeding four consumer threads.

concepts.definition: Many concurrent readers, exclusive writer.
concepts.detection_hint: RWLock/sync.RWMutex/parking_lot RwLock; read-locks around getters, write-locks around mutations.
concepts.example: sync.RWMutex protecting a shared cache.

concepts.definition: Recursively split work, run subtasks in parallel, join results.
concepts.detection_hint: ForkJoinPool; recursive task classes; parallel streams/divide-and-conquer with a merge step.
concepts.example: RecursiveTask splitting an array sum until threshold.

concepts.definition: Isolated actors with private state communicating only via async messages.
concepts.detection_hint: Actor/mailbox abstractions; receive loops; spawn; no shared mutable state between actors.
concepts.example: Akka/Erlang actors exchanging immutable messages.

concepts.definition: Processes synchronize by passing values through typed channels.
concepts.detection_hint: chan/select/<- constructs; channel-based pipelines; goroutines communicating via channels not shared memory.
concepts.example: Go pipeline: gen -> sq -> sink connected by channels.

concepts.definition: Placeholder for an async result, composable via then/await.
concepts.detection_hint: Promise/Future types; async/await; .then chains; CompletableFuture composition.
concepts.example: await fetch(url) then JSON.parse the body.

concepts.definition: Concurrent tasks scoped to a lexical block that exits only when all children finish.
concepts.detection_hint: TaskGroup/coroutineScope/nursery APIs; flag orphaned spawn without a scope handle.
concepts.example: async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: tg.create_task(...) x3.

concepts.definition: Idle workers steal tasks from busy workers' deques for load balance.
concepts.detection_hint: Deque-per-worker pools; ForkJoinPool/rayon/TBB runtimes; usually runtime-level rather than app code.
concepts.example: Java ForkJoinPool rebalancing recursive tasks across cores.

concepts.definition: Nodes agree on a single coordinator via consensus or leases.
concepts.detection_hint: Election client libs (etcd/ZooKeeper leases); campaign/elect calls; leader-check guards before writes.
concepts.example: Cron workers electing one leader to run the nightly job.

concepts.definition: Classic fault-tolerant consensus: proposers, acceptors, learners agreeing via quorum-majority prepare/accept phases.
concepts.detection_hint: Usually via libraries; quorum config; acceptor/proposer roles; Multi-Paxos impls.
concepts.example: Multi-Paxos agreeing a replicated log sequence.

concepts.definition: Understandable consensus: leader election plus log replication with terms, heartbeats, majority commit.
concepts.detection_hint: Raft libraries (etcd raft, hashicorp/raft); term/index fields; AppendEntries/RequestVote RPCs.
concepts.example: etcd cluster replicating the KV log via Raft.

concepts.definition: Per-node counters tracking causality across replicas to detect concurrent edits.
concepts.detection_hint: Version maps {nodeId: counter} attached to records; conflict-resolution merge functions.
concepts.example: Riak-style vclocks detecting concurrent cart updates.

concepts.definition: Nodes periodically exchange state with random peers; epidemic dissemination.
concepts.detection_hint: Periodic peer-exchange loops; membership lists (SWIM); fanout config.
concepts.example: Cassandra nodes gossiping membership every second.

concepts.definition: Hash ring mapping keys to nodes so rebalancing moves minimal data.
concepts.detection_hint: Ring/vnode structures; hash(key) over a ring; virtual-node counts.
concepts.example: Memcached/Dynamo-style key distribution over a hash ring.

concepts.definition: Coordinator asks participants to prepare, then commits or aborts atomically across nodes.
concepts.detection_hint: XA transactions; prepare/commit RPC pairs; transaction-coordinator components.
concepts.example: Distributed DB commit via XA prepare then commit.

concepts.definition: Reads/writes succeed when R + W > N nodes respond, trading consistency vs availability.
concepts.detection_hint: QUORUM consistency levels; N/R/W config in Cassandra/Riak/Dynamo-style stores.
concepts.example: N=3, W=2, R=2 gives strong consistency per operation.

concepts.definition: Incremental, error-tolerant parser generator and runtime producing a concrete syntax tree with one unified API across 40+ language grammars; the single horizontal answer to 'parse every language'.
concepts.match_power: Structural S-expression queries with named nodes, fields, captures, quantifiers (+, *, ?), alternation, and predicates (#eq?, #match?, #any-of?).
concepts.transform_power: None natively (parse and locate only); edits are applied externally to the source text using captured ranges.
concepts.notes: Foundation of the god-mode architecture (option a). Error tolerance means it parses half-written code, which is exactly the pre-edit-hook situation. Incremental re-parsing makes per-edit re-analysis sub-millisecond.

concepts.definition: S-expression pattern language over tree-sitter trees: (call function: (identifier) @fn (#eq? @fn "print")) @hit — one matching dialect for every language.
concepts.match_power: Node kinds, anonymous tokens, field constraints, captures, wildcards, quantifiers, anchors, and predicates for value equality and regex on text.
concepts.transform_power: None; capture locations are handed to an external rewriter.
concepts.notes: The lingua franca the universal rule schema compiles into. Grammar node names differ per language; framework profiles normalize the differences.

concepts.definition: Complete match-and-rewrite engine built on tree-sitter: CLI plus napi/PyO3 bindings, YAML rule files, per-language pattern syntax with metavariables ($VAR, $$$ARGS), and first-class fix templates.
concepts.match_power: Pattern matching plus composable rule logic (all/any/not), relational rules (inside, has, follows, precedes), kind/regex/strictness selectors.
concepts.transform_power: First-class fix: templates that substitute captured metavariables; diff-apply CLI; usable for real auto-fix in the rule schema.
concepts.notes: The single best foundation for the tool: one YAML rule format for every language, so the E4 universal schema compiles directly to it. Rust core — embeddable in the single binary.

concepts.definition: Static analysis with a language-agnostic pattern DSL ($METAVARS, ... ellipses, pattern-inside/-not/-either), semantic equivalences (constant propagation, import aliasing), taint mode (sources to sinks), and a huge community rule registry.
concepts.match_power: Very high: generic patterns plus intra/inter-procedural taint tracking; Pro tier adds cross-function and cross-file analysis.
concepts.transform_power: Per-rule autofix templates; good for point fixes, weaker for large refactors than dedicated codemod tools.
concepts.notes: Second match engine for secret/security/taint rule kinds in the universal schema. OSS engine runs fully local; Assistant/Supply Chain are cloud.

languages: language-agnostic via generic balanced-delimiter parsers; tuned parsers for ~20 including c
concepts.definition: Lightweight structural match-and-rewrite over syntax shapes with holes (:[var]) — no real AST required, usable as a one-liner CLI.
concepts.match_power: Medium: structural but not semantically precise (no name or type resolution); excellent for 'looks like X' shapes.
concepts.transform_power: High for its class: match/rewrite templates with hole substitution; fast enough for repo-wide one-shot migrations.
concepts.notes: The 'good enough in 5 minutes' codemod; ideal fallback for languages with no mature native tooling.

concepts.definition: Meta's codemod runner over Babel/TypeScript/Recast ASTs; scripts traverse and mutate a Collection of nodes and re-print formatting-preserving output via recast.
concepts.match_power: AST traversal with typed Collection filters (find CallExpressions, filter by callee name); type-awareness only if wired to the TS checker manually.
concepts.transform_power: High: node builders/replacement with diff-minimal output; the battle-tested standard for React/Meta-scale migrations.
concepts.notes: Reach for it only when ast-grep fixes are insufficient (complex API migrations); pairs with recast.

concepts.definition: JavaScript AST pretty-printer that preserves original formatting for untouched code, enabling diff-minimal transforms.
concepts.match_power: None (printer, not matcher).
concepts.transform_power: High as infrastructure: any AST edit re-prints only the changed nodes with original style retained.
concepts.notes: The formatting-preservation layer under jscodeshift; the property every deep-dive fixer should borrow.

concepts.definition: Ergonomic high-level wrapper over the official TypeScript Compiler API: full type checker, symbol resolution, project-wide rename/move/extract.
concepts.match_power: Very high when type-aware: 'find all references of this typed symbol', inheritance queries, diagnostics access.
concepts.transform_power: High: structured source-file manipulation APIs (insert/replace/rename) with formatting control.
concepts.notes: Chameleon's TS parser. Use as a lazy deep-dive adapter for rules that declare needs: [types].

concepts.definition: The official TypeScript compiler as a library: scanner, parser, binder, type checker, emitter — the deepest possible TS/JS program model.
concepts.match_power: Total within TS/JS: full type resolution, control flow, symbol tables.
concepts.transform_power: Via transformers/printer; commonly wrapped by ts-morph for ergonomics.
concepts.notes: Canonical example of option (b) cost: deep but one language per integration.

concepts.definition: Lossless semantic refactoring at scale for the JVM: auto-refactoring recipes over a fully type-attributed Lossless Semantic Tree, composable and idempotent, with Maven/Gradle plugins and a large public recipe catalog.
concepts.match_power: Type-aware visitor matching over attributed trees (find usages of a method by fully-qualified signature).
concepts.transform_power: Best-in-class for Java: lossless, idempotent recipe application; the tool real Spring/Quarkus migrations are written in.
concepts.notes: Declarative YAML recipes + Java visitors; the model for what 'review-required' codemod-script fixes look like in the JVM.

concepts.definition: Source-level Java metamodel (CtModel) for analysis and transformation with position-preserving pretty printing.
concepts.match_power: High: model queries, filters, and template matching over a typed Java metamodel.
concepts.transform_power: High: direct metamodel mutation with source-faithful output.
concepts.notes: Research-grade alternative to OpenRewrite for bespoke Java transforms.

concepts.definition: Meta's Concrete Syntax Tree for Python: preserves every comment, whitespace, and formatting detail, enabling lossless codemods with a matcher DSL (m.Match/m.Find) and codemod framework.
concepts.match_power: Precise node-pattern matchers including decorators and annotations; semantics limited to syntax (no type inference).
concepts.transform_power: High: lossless transforms with comments intact; the gold standard for Python codemods.
concepts.notes: Chameleon's Python parser. Backend for py.* review-required auto-fixes (e.g., print-to-logger).

concepts.definition: Meta's refactoring framework on fissix/lib2to3 for composing multi-step Python refactors with query/filter/modify pipelines.
concepts.match_power: Medium: pattern-based selectors over lib2to3 grammars (legacy grammar limits modern syntax).
concepts.transform_power: Medium-high: composable interactive refactors at scale.
concepts.notes: Legacy-grammar caveat; prefer libcst for new Python codemods.

concepts.definition: Opinionated auto-modernizer that upgrades Python code to newer syntax (f-strings, PEP 604 unions, typing rewrites) with --py3x-plus targeting.
concepts.match_power: Narrow: fixed catalog of modernization patterns.
concepts.transform_power: High within its catalog; safe, idempotent rewrites.
concepts.notes: Model of a 'safety: safe' auto-fix: deterministic, low-risk, runs in post-edit verify.

concepts.definition: The AST library under RuboCop: uniform Ruby node model with a compact node-pattern DSL ((send nil? :puts ...)) for expressing Ruby idiom shapes.
concepts.match_power: Expressive node patterns for Ruby idioms; no type information (Ruby's dynamism caps static certainty).
concepts.transform_power: Via RuboCop's AutoCorrector range edits.
concepts.notes: Pattern-based rather than type-based; pairs with syntax_tree/Prism.

concepts.definition: Prism-backed Ruby parsing, formatting, and inspection toolkit (syntax_tree gem): lossless-ish printing and node search APIs.
concepts.match_power: Node search plus visitor traversal over the Prism tree.
concepts.transform_power: Formatting and structured rewriting; used for reformat codemods.
concepts.notes: Built on the same Prism parser Chameleon uses for Ruby.

concepts.definition: The official modern Ruby parser (default in CRuby 3.4+): error-tolerant, portable C library with Ruby bindings, replacing ripper.
concepts.match_power: Full-fidelity syntax trees; matching via visitors or rubocop-ast patterns.
concepts.transform_power: None natively; consumed by syntax_tree and RuboCop.
concepts.notes: Chameleon's Ruby parser; error tolerance makes it hook-friendly like tree-sitter.

concepts.definition: Ruby's dominant linter/formatter with hundreds of cops, auto-correction, and a custom-cop API on rubocop-ast node patterns.
concepts.match_power: Node-pattern DSL plus on_send/on_def hooks per cop.
concepts.transform_power: Auto-correct via AutoCorrector for many cops.

concepts.definition: Microsoft's .NET Compiler Platform: the C# compiler as an API with syntax trees, semantic model (symbols, types, dataflow), diagnostics, and a code-fix/refactoring SDK.
concepts.match_power: Full semantic queries: ISymbol resolution, dataflow analysis, workspace-wide operations.
concepts.transform_power: High: SyntaxRewriter, DocumentEditor, formatting-preserving document changes.

concepts.transform_power: Fix providers for most diagnostics.

concepts.transform_power: None natively (report only); fixes via rector separately.

concepts.transform_power: Correction producers via dart fix and analysis-server plugins.

schema.title: Universal Rule — one schema for every concept kind, all languages

kind.description: The taxonomy concept kind this rule encodes

languages.description: tree-sitter language ids; empty array = language-agnostic

archetypes.description: Archetype names from the archetype engine; ["*"] = repo-wide

mode.description: Per-rule override of global mode; enforce refused below calibrated threshold

engine.description: coupling/git-diff dispatch to the code-intelligence layer over the change set, not the parse layer

rule.description: Engine-native rule body: ast-grep YAML, semgrep YAML, S-expression, regex, or coupling predicate

needs.description: Routes rule to a lazy native deep-dive adapter (ts-morph, go/packages, rust-analyzer, Roslyn) when semantics required

message.description: One-line verdict shown to the AI/human

rationale.description: Why the rule exists; injected into agent context

good_example.description: Real conforming snippet mined from the canonical witness

counterexample.description: Real violating line/span mined from the repo (highest-centrality offender)
